messages:
maria.g: Heads-up — customer (customer-inc-prod) reports rerank responses are coming back in the wrong order after upgrading to ts-sdk@2.4.1. They say the score values in the request payload look odd. Repro attached below.

alex.k: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the exact request payload + SDK call + request_id if available? Also which model/version and endpoint?

maria.g: request_id: rq_0a9b3c, model: rerank-alpha-v1, endpoint: /v1/rerank. Minimal repro (from their app, TypeScript):

```ts
// simplified client call from customer
import { RedwoodRerankClient } from '@redwood/inference-ts';
const client = new RedwoodRerankClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
const candidates = ["A","B","C"];
const scores = [0.842, 0.123, 0.559];
await client.rerank({ query: "find docs", candidates, scores });
```

But when we inspect the raw HTTP payload on the wire (captured by their proxy) we see:

```json
{"query":"find docs","candidates":["A","B","C"],"scores":["0,842","0,123","0,559"]}
```

So scores are strings with commas as decimal separators. Server logs then show parse warnings and fallback ordering.

customer-inc-prod: we had no other changes besides bumping ts-sdk. Pinning back to 2.3.9 seemed to fix it for us.

alex.k: OK that points to a client-side serialization bug in the TS SDK. Can eng reproduce?

jeremy.eng: I can reproduce locally by forcing a German locale. Looks like a bug in utils/formatScores introduced in 2.4.0 — the function calls Number.prototype.toLocaleString() for a logging/formatting pass, but it mutates the array and returns strings when code mistakenly assigns the result back into the request object. In environments with comma decimal separators (e.g., de-DE) that yields "0,842" strings in the JSON body.

Repro steps I used:
1) node --icu-data-dir=... (or system locale set to de-DE)
2) run the minimal snippet with ts-sdk@2.4.1
3) capture outgoing request -> scores are strings with commas

Stack pointer: packages/ts-sdk/src/utils/formatScores.ts line ~42. The call does:

```ts
const pretty = scores.map(n => n.toLocaleString());
requestBody.scores = pretty as any; // <-- bug: overwrites numeric array with strings
```

Fix: do not replace numeric array; if a pretty/log string is needed keep a separate field or use toFixed/Number for canonical serialization. I'll open ENG-9876 and PR to stop using toLocaleString in the payload path.

jeremy.eng: Server-side defensive change: I've added a quick parse guard in the rerank endpoint to reject non-numeric score values (and log the raw incoming value) instead of silently coercing. That will help catch similar regressions for other SDKs.

alex.k: Great. For support/helping the customer: recommend pinning to ts-sdk@2.3.9 and restarting, and ask them to confirm they see numeric scores in the captured payload. Also escalate to customer success for a brief incident note.

maria.g: Sent the pin instruction — customer confirms they're back to correct ordering after pin. I'll share the request_id if they reproduce after the next deploy.

support-bot: Ticket ENG-9876 created and assigned to jeremy.eng for SDK fix, PR pending. SLA: P2. :eyes:

jeremy.eng: PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2345 — change is small, unit tests added for locales. I'll land after getting a quick review. Then we'll cut a 2.4.2 patch and a changelog note.

alex.k: Thanks everyone. Add a line to the KB: "If rerank returns unexpected order after ts-sdk upgrade, check for non-numeric score serialization (locale formatting). Workaround: pin to 2.3.9." :thumbsup:

maria.g: 👍 closing the loop with the customer now.

customer-inc-prod: thank you for the quick turnaround!
